solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Add space for tribal symbol

parts.note: to tot up is to add figures
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave room on a page for some tribal emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved pole or emblem representing a clan's spirit ancestor is a classic tribal symbol.

clue.text: Ring chemists about hospital charging points

parts.note: to ring a bell is to toll it

indicators.note: the chemists' name sits around the hospital letter

parts.note: Boots is a British chain of chemists' shops

explanation.surface: Someone phones pharmacies asking about the hospital's car-park charging points.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTS is a British high-street chemist chain. 'Charging points' looks like electric-car chargers, but it means places where a charge is levied.
explanation.definitionFit: Booths on roads or bridges are where drivers are charged a fee, hence charging points.

clue.text: VAT has group of teachers upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the group's letters are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: A teachers' union is upset about value added tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT in capitals suggests the British tax, but here it is simply a large container.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask for wine or beer is a vat.

clue.text: Man Ray originally capturing hotel barman

indicators.note: the word for man holds the hotel letter inside it

parts.note: a man is a male
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of Ray

explanation.surface: The photographer Man Ray takes a picture of a hotel bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man Ray' reads as the surrealist photographer but splits into two pieces. 'Barman' is a pun: a composer is a man of musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav the Austrian composer wrote music in bars, so he is jokingly a bar man.

clue.text: Opponents welcome old man to first course

indicators.note: the opponents take in the old man, so his letters go inside

parts.note: antis are people opposed to something
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Even one's adversaries greet father warmly as the meal starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian appetisers of cured meats and olives are served as the opening course of a meal.

clue.text: A police department controls drug users

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
to head something is to lead or control it

explanation.surface: A police unit is in charge of tackling drug addicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for habitual takers of LSD, so users of a particular drug.

clue.text: Character in Greek article volunteers

parts.note: the definite article
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a Greek figure who signs up to volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character, in the sense of a written symbol.

clue.text: Pick brief lecture arranged during afternoon

indicators.note: the rearranged lecture goes within the afternoon letters

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, is the afternoon

indicators.note: arranged means the shortened word's letters are put in a new order
brief means the word lecture loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A short talk is scheduled for some time after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a verb meaning choose, but it is the noun for a guitarist's plucking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist's pick is the small flat tool used to pluck strings.

clue.text: Cold stall in Billingsgate?

parts.note: a market stall is a stand
Billingsgate is London's fish market, so anything there is of fish

explanation.surface: A refrigerated market stall at a London fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market; the question mark flags that its wares are described rather than defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof and unfriendly keeps people at a distance, which is what being cold means.

clue.text: Completed deliveries at Old Trafford

definitions.meaning: finished, as in 'the game is done'
Old Trafford is a Manchester cricket ground; a set of six balls bowled is a unit of cricket

explanation.surface: Parcels were delivered to the football stadium and the job finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford suggests Manchester United's football ground, but there is also a Test cricket ground of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: When something has ended it is finished, a common adjectival sense.

clue.text: Put to sea without a periodical break

indicators.note: without means the letter A is removed

parts.note: to launch a boat is to put it to sea
Time is a weekly news magazine

explanation.surface: Sailors heading out to sea with no magazine to read.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday pause from work for a meal is a break in the working day.

clue.text: Steer clear of woman screening commercial

indicators.note: Eve hides the commercial within her name

parts.note: Eve, the first woman
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Someone dodges a woman who is showing an advert on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or keep away from it.

clue.text: Inconsolable, destitute? Then read novel

parts.note: broke means having no money

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of 'Then read' are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone penniless and grieving is advised to read a novel for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelmed by grief or sorrow and unable to be comforted.

clue.text: Wobbly cobblestones bishop avoided on the way out

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order
avoided means one bishop letter is left out

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop steps around loose cobbles as he leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided' takes one B out of COBBLESTONES; 'Wobbly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming outdated and falling out of use, so going out of fashion.

clue.text: College Times tarnishes investment agencies

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
T is an abbreviation for time, so times gives two of them
rusts means corrodes or tarnishes

explanation.surface: A university reports that a newspaper is damaging the reputation of fund managers.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective funds that pool investors' money are run by financial firms, hence investment agencies.

clue.text: Bring down set of books to entertain me and my family?

indicators.note: the books host the family pronoun inside them

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
a speaker with family says us

explanation.surface: Someone buys a book set to amuse themselves and relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow or remove from power is to bring down, as with a government.

clue.text: Ruffian prepared to collar school urchin

indicators.note: the reworked ruffian grabs the school, holding it inside
prepared means the letters of ruffian are made up afresh

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A thug is ready to grab a schoolboy rascal by the collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but GAM, a school of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruffy, ragged child of the streets is an urchin.

clue.text: Terrified heading into a fight

indicators.note: the direction goes inside the article and the fight

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrum
west is a compass heading

explanation.surface: Someone scared stiff while being pitched into a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with awe or dread, so frightened.

clue.text: A brick-carrier cuts short period in plant

indicators.note: the hod goes into the shortened period, splitting it
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A builder's labourer trims down time spent at a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' could be a factory in the surface, but it is the flower; the hod-carrier's tool cuts into the shortened period.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily-family flower of Greek myth, said to cover the Elysian Fields, is a plant.

clue.text: Odd bits of fossils collected by top kinswoman

indicators.note: the selected letters are gathered inside the top

parts.note: a halter is a type of women's top

indicators.note: odd bits are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of fossils

explanation.surface: A relative in a fancy top picks up fossil fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister sharing one parent is a female relative, so a kinswoman.

clue.text: Invent noun with German cases

indicators.note: the German word encases the noun abbreviation

parts.note: mit is German for with
N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about German nouns and their cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like grammatical case, but it is a verb: encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a new word or phrase is to invent it.

clue.text: Lawyer discarded shot

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney
shed means cast off

explanation.surface: A lawyer is thrown out after being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are ruined or wrecked are said to be shot, in the slang sense.

clue.text: Miss beginning to scoff her chocolate spread

indicators.note: the beginning of scoff is its first letter
spread means the letters of 'her chocolate' are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman starts wolfing down her chocolate spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' is the form of address pupils use for their teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils address a female teacher as Miss, so Miss stands for her.

clue.text: Top in the Open, or missing the cut

indicators.note: the word or is cut out and is missing from the longer word

parts.note: outdoor describes things done in the open air
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer leads the Open Championship, or else fails to make the cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf terms mislead: 'the Open' gives OUTDOOR, and 'missing the cut' drops the OR from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: Hilary's one expression

definitions.meaning: Hilary is the spring session at Oxford University and the law courts
a word or phrase, as in a technical expression

explanation.surface: Someone named Hilary has a favourite expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person's name but is the name of a university and legal session.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase used for something is an expression, as in a term of abuse.

clue.text: Editor brings in people to do his work

indicators.note: the editor's letters surround the people

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: An editor hires staff to do his job for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Correcting and revising text is exactly an editor's job, hence his work.

clue.text: Bottle hard water in Scotland

parts.note: tough means hard
Loch Ness is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A bottle of hard Scottish water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for nerve or courage, a sense shared with grit and resilience.

clue.text: Wood essential to barrel-maker

indicators.note: essential means inner, so the letters sit inside barrel-maker

explanation.surface: A cooper relies on good timber for his barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous tree whose timber is a familiar wood.

clue.text: Mike and others handle casting perhaps

parts.note: M is Mike in the radio alphabet
et al is Latin shorthand for and others
to work something is to handle or manipulate it

explanation.surface: Mike and his friends take charge of the auditions for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' suggests choosing actors, but here it is pouring molten iron into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast iron object is an example of craft in iron and other hard materials.

clue.text: Party's hosting last of rhythm and blues

indicators.note: the party's letters contain the picked letter

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, plus the S

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of rhythm

explanation.surface: A party features a rhythm and blues band to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhythm and blues' reads as a music genre, but 'blues' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the dumps means low spirits, the same mood as having the blues.
